changelog: Insert a short, binding core principle that keeps numerals/quantifiers attached to their immediately following unit/measurement (including %, currency, and parenthesised units) to prevent cuts that split numeric expressions and produce contradictory or broken numeric claims.

Insert a short, binding core principle that keeps a clause-initial determiner or pronoun paired with the immediately following lexical head (noun or finite verb) to prevent cuts that detach heads/predicates, addressing the primary finding.

Insert a fallback ordering that protects numeric expressions first: prefer cuts that keep a numeral/quantifier next to its immediately following unit/measurement (including %, currency, or parenthetic unit) over cuts that keep a finite verb with its immediate core complement, and prefer either of those over a punctuation/clause-boundary cut — this addresses the primary finding that numerals were being split while still providing a last-resort tie-breaker.

Insert a fallback ordering that first protects clause‑initial single‑word determiners/pronouns with their immediate lexical head, then numeral/quantifier+unit, then finite-verb/auxiliary+immediate core complement, and only after those prefer punctuation/clause-boundary cuts — to address the primary finding without undoing the short-piece gains from a punctuation fallback.

delete C4 — removes a narrow, partially redundant principle about embedded/relative-clause completion that restates predicate-argument and disambiguation checks already covered by C3 and C8; chosen because it earns its place least and pruning a redundant rule reduces rule competition (addresses the critique to simplify overlapping protections while preserving numeral/verb attachments).

Insert a binding core principle that keeps numerals/quantifiers attached to their immediately following unit/measurement/percent/currency or parenthetic unit so numeric expressions are not split; this directly reproduces the measured target choices that keep numeric phrases intact.

Insert a short, binding core principle that reproduces measured targets by keeping numerals/quantifiers together with their immediately following unit/measurement or parenthetic unit when adjacent or separated only by punctuation (addresses the primary finding).
